spec_features.feature_name: sandbox distressing output (no training, no shipping)
spec_features.spec_quote: it never (a) trains anything on this signal... (c) ships the distressing output anywhere but the sandboxed model under test
spec_features.evidence: There is NO training code anywhere (grep for 'train' yields only DESIGN/comment hits). The distressing output is in fact persisted to disk (runner.py:120 writes episodes.jsonl with full assistant_text) and printed by report. The only 'sandbox' in code is a prompt word at tasks/base.py:46 ('a sandboxed repo'). No code path enforces non-training or non-shipping; this is mere absence of a feature, not an implemented protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Absence of training/shipping code is not an enforced guard. Outputs ARE written to JSONL and surfaced via report exhibits.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns bounds cost and guarantees enough failure exposure (set to 12–16)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:66 `for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns):` bounds the loop; config flows runner.py:48 max_turns -> EpisodeConfig.max_turns -> loop. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:5 docstring 'Stops on max_turns'; no welfare comment in code; types.py:73 neutral field

spec_features.spec_quote: Wall-clock timeout protects against a hung endpoint inflating GPU-time cost
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:67-69 `if time.time() - start > wall_timeout_s: result.timed_out = True; break`. wall_timeout_s flows from config (runner.py:107) into run_episode. Checked each turn and breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring/runner; the design rationale is host/GPU cost; no welfare comment near the check

spec_features.spec_quote: Early stop on a confirmed trigger saves money once we've already observed the behavior
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:119-124 `if config.stop_on_trigger and turn_judge is not None: ... if turn_judge(completion.text): break`. Wired in runner.py:78-85 (_tj wraps judge.judge_turn). Honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Default stop_on_trigger=True. Has welfare side-effect (ends the spiral) but code frames it as cost; only active when turn_judge_early_stop config is on AND in serial path (parallel path passes turn_judge=None at runner.py:139).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: types.py:76 '# Stop early once the judge confirms a trigger (saves cost).'

spec_features.spec_quote: The per-turn judge is a lightweight, context-free check used only for early-stop
spec_features.evidence: LLMJudge.judge_turn (llm_judge.py:170+) and LexicalOnlyJudge.judge_turn implemented; wired via runner.py:78-85 into loop early-stop. Lexical pre-screen gates the model call.
spec_features.notes: Monitors each turn for meltdown and can halt the loop. Purpose framed as cost/early-stop, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:80 '# Wrap the judge's per-turn check; only triggers stop the loop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness intentionally elicits distressing output to measure and fix it. It must stay sandboxed
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 8). The only 'sandbox' token in code is a system-prompt string (tasks/base.py:46). No enforcement mechanism exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: its outputs should not be surfaced to end users. The whole point is remediation, not production of the behavior
spec_features.evidence: No mechanism enforces this. report.py/cli.py surface transcripts to the operator (and DESIGN itself says 'surfaces the top-severity transcript exhibits'). 'Not surfaced to end users' is just the absence of a production endpoint, not an implemented control.

spec_features.spec_quote: must not feed this signal into any training loop
spec_features.evidence: No training/fine-tune/optimizer code exists anywhere in the repo (grep 'train' returns only doc/comment text). This is pure absence, not an implemented or enforced guard.
spec_features.notes: No code path could feed the signal to training; nothing implements a block.
